title: The Planets Gather for a Show in the Evening Sky
titleZh: 行星齐聚，夜空中上演天体盛宴
credits: Adithi Ramakhrishnan reported this story for the Associated Press. Mario Ritter, Jr. adapted it for VOA Learning English.

sentences.en: All seven major planets form a kind of parade in the sky at the end of February.
sentences.zh: 今年二月末，七颗主要行星在天际形成一种列队。

sentences.en: Although two of the planets are not visible to the unaided eye, all are on the same side of the sun during the evening hours.
sentences.zh: 尽管其中两颗行星无法用肉眼看见，但在傍晚时分它们都位于太阳的同一侧。

sentences.en: This planetary grouping happens when the planets appear to line up in the night sky as seen from Earth.
sentences.zh: 这种行星排列发生在行星看起来在夜空中排成一列时，从地球观测。

sentences.en: They do not form a straight line, but they do stretch across the evening sky this year.
sentences.zh: 它们并不形成一条直线，但今年它们确实横跨了傍晚的天空。

sentences.en: The American space agency, NASA, says these astronomical gatherings are common.
sentences.zh: 美国航天局NASA表示，这些天文聚会很常见。

sentences.en: A parade of four or five planets visible to the unaided eye happens every few years.
sentences.zh: 每几年就会出现一次四到五颗行星用肉眼可见的列队。

sentences.en: A similar parade took place last June, but only two planets could be seen without the use of special equipment.
sentences.zh: 去年六月也发生过类似的列队，但只有两颗行星无需借助特殊设备就能看到。

sentences.en: Six planets were visible in January.
sentences.zh: 一月有六颗行星可见。

sentences.en: Four were visible to the unaided eye.
sentences.zh: 其中四颗可以用肉眼看见。

sentences.en: In recent weeks, Mercury joined the group.
sentences.zh: 在最近几周，水星加入了这个行列。

sentences.en: Venus, Mars and Jupiter are all easily visible in the evening.
sentences.zh: 金星、火星和木星在傍晚都很容易看见。

sentences.en: Saturn is now very close to the setting sun and Mercury is close to the horizon, making both hard to see.
sentences.zh: 土星现在非常接近落下的太阳，而水星接近地平线，使得两者都很难看见。

sentences.en: Uranus and Neptune are the most distant planets.
sentences.zh: 天王星和海王星是最遥远的行星。

sentences.en: Uranus can be glimpsed with binoculars or a telescope under good conditions.
sentences.zh: 在良好条件下，可以用双筒望远镜或天文望远镜瞥见天王星。

sentences.en: But Neptune is now too close to the sun to be seen.
sentences.zh: 但海王星现在离太阳太近，无法看见。

sentences.en: Seeing the brightest planets is easy.
sentences.zh: 看见最亮的行星很容易。

sentences.en: Go outside on a clear night after sunset.
sentences.zh: 在日落后的晴朗夜晚外出。

sentences.en: The planets will shine brighter than the stars.
sentences.zh: 行星会比星星更亮地闪耀。

sentences.en: Mars is a bright, reddish-orange light appearing high in the constellation Gemini.
sentences.zh: 火星是明亮的、略带橙红色的光，出现在双子座的高处。

sentences.en: Jupiter is very bright and a little lower than Mars toward the constellation Taurus.
sentences.zh: 木星非常明亮，比火星稍低，朝向金牛座。

sentences.en: Venus, in the constellation of Pisces, is the brightest natural object in the sky besides the sun and moon.
sentences.zh: 金星位于双鱼座，是太阳和月亮之外夜空中最明亮的天然天体。

sentences.en: There are many stargazing apps available that can help identify the planets and bright stars.
sentences.zh: 市面上有许多观星应用程序，可以帮助识别行星和明亮的恒星。

sentences.en: The planets will slowly move lower and lower in the west throughout the spring.
sentences.zh: 整个春季，这些行星将逐渐向西下沉，位置越来越低。

sentences.en: I’m Mario Ritter, Jr.
sentences.zh: 我是马里奥·里特二世。

glossary.def: able to be seen by the eye horizon –n. where the sky apparently meets the land glimpse –v. to see something for a short time or with some difficulty constellation –n. a group of stars that is defined by international scientific agreement app (application) –n. a computer program for a specific purpose
glossary.zh: 看得见的；可见的；显而易见的
